content.text: Section 8 is fully aligned with our preferred position, so no redline is needed.

input.quote: 8.2 Each Order Form has the initial term stated in it and thereafter renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal. Vendor shall remind Customer of an upcoming renewal at least sixty days beforehand.
input.rationale: Renewal terms are twelve months (not multi-year), and only Customer needs to act to opt out, with a thirty-day non-renewal notice window — at or better than the preferred 30-day threshold. Vendor must send a renewal reminder sixty days in advance, and missing the reminder extends Customer's opt-out deadline, which is more favourable than the playbook requires. Section 8.3 caps renewal uplift at the lesser of CPI and three percent, with ninety days' notice and no increase on prepaid periods, matching the preferred cap. Section 7 contains no separate renewal escalator (7.1 fixes Fees during the initial term). The three-year figure in 8.1 is the master agreement term, not an automatic multi-year renewal, so the walk-away trigger is not implicated.
